newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says Iraq must pull troops out of Kurdish area.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says Iraq must pull troops out of Kurdish area.

text.p: Germany said on Tuesday it expected Baghdad to pull its troops out of the north of Iraq at once and stop attacks on Kurdish civilians, following U.S. missile strikes against Iraqi military targets.
"The federal government expects that everything will be done in the current situation to avoid an escalation," government spokesman Peter Hausmann said.
"In particular, it expects Iraq to withdraw its troops immediately and completely and cease all use of violence against the Kurdish civilian population."
Hausmann was visiting Kiev with Chancellor Helmut Kohl. His comments to reporters were also released in Bonn.
Hausmann added that Germany had from the outset condemned Iraq's incursion into the United Nations-implemented no-fly zone in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq.
"Therefore the government has full understanding for today's American reaction," he said.
Earlier, Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said the U.S. cruise missile attacks against targets in Iraq were an "appropriate and justified" response to Iraq's military attacks against Kurds in the north.
